aws-bill-drop.label: data-platform AWS spend after moving to Google Cloud
aws-bill-drop.method: Monthly AWS invoices for the data account, peak (July 2023) vs October 2026 (indexed 100 → 1.4), after migrating data workloads to Google Cloud.

viz.caption: Monthly data AWS spend, indexed to 100 at peak

bq-slot-cut.label: reserved BigQuery slot capacity after workload split
bq-slot-cut.method: Baseline BigQuery slot reservation before vs after moving BI traffic to on-demand billing with a daily scan quota (indexed 100 → 50).

viz.caption: Reserved BigQuery slot capacity, indexed to 100

warehouse-compression.label: billable warehouse storage footprint via physical compression
warehouse-compression.method: Physical (compressed) footprint vs logical bytes in BigQuery table-storage metadata across the data warehouse (indexed 100 logical → 16.5 physical, ~6× compression).

viz.caption: Logical size vs. compressed footprint, by area

model-pruning.label: AutoGluon model artifact size after ensemble pruning
model-pruning.method: Combined artifact size across four production AutoGluon models before vs after pruning sub-models unused by the final ensemble (indexed 100 → 29; up to −83% on individual ensembles), with identical predictions on validation samples.

viz.caption: Combined AutoGluon model artifact footprint, indexed to 100

model-release-quarters.label: of quarters since joining JULO with a new ML model version going live
model-release-quarters.method: Quarters from 2021 Q4 to 2026 Q4 in which at least one new model version made its first production prediction, from the company's inventory of every production model version (19 of 21 quarters; real-time in 17, batch in 15). Placeholder and rule-only versions are excluded.

medallion-docs.label: of medallion warehouse columns documented in code
medallion-docs.method: Share of declared columns across the medallion dbt manifest that carry a non-empty description pushed into BigQuery table metadata.

semantic-dashboard-share.label: of governed semantic-layer queries run via saved dashboards
semantic-dashboard-share.method: Share of non-SQL Metabase query executions against the semantic-layer gold tables served through saved questions and dashboards (the remaining 5.9% are ad-hoc visual explorations, all without writing SQL).

viz.caption: 94.1% via saved questions & dashboards, 5.9% ad-hoc visual queries

cdc-cloud-migration.label: of registered CDC tables actively streaming to BigQuery
cdc-cloud-migration.method: Share of tables in the CDC registry actively replicated from Postgres logical replication slots into BigQuery on Google Cloud, with 100% of streamers migrated off Alibaba Cloud.

underwriting-cutover.label: of real-time underwriting traffic migrated off the legacy monolith
underwriting-cutover.method: Share of production loan-application scoring traffic routed through the new event-driven orchestrator and containerised model services after shadow validation and proxy cutover.

deploy-coverage.label: of the data team's service repos deploy through the self-service deploy platform
deploy-coverage.method: Service repos registered in the central deployment registry out of the data team's repos that run a service (8 of 9). The remaining one is a legacy service still on another team's pipeline.

viz.caption: 88 of every 100 service repos deploy through the platform (filled)

metabase-managed-access.label: of Metabase access sits in groups the self-service data-ops platform creates and manages
metabase-managed-access.method: Group memberships of active non-admin Metabase users, in groups the data-ops platform provisions, out of all their memberships beyond the default group, from Metabase's own database.

viz.caption: Every Metabase access group in use is platform-managed

two-person-team.label: of my time at JULO with a data engineering team of just two engineers
two-person-team.method: Days since I joined on which no third data engineer was on the team. Each former data engineer's time on the team is estimated from their first and last commit in the platform's main repository. People usually join before their first commit and leave after their last, so the true share is likely lower.

commit-share.label: of the data team's code changes since I joined are mine
commit-share.method: Non-merge commits across the 11 repositories the data team owns, from git history on all branches. Bots and shared machine accounts are excluded, each person's commit identities are merged, and my personal notebook repository is left out. The rest: 46.5% by other data engineers, past and present, and 10.3% by other teams.

viz.caption: Share of non-merge commits to the data team's repositories, by author
